biography: César Vianna, a name once whispered with reverence in the Brazilian stock car scene, hails from the sun-baked streets of Ribeirão Preto. His journey began not in a kart, but behind the wheel of his father's beat-up Passat, delivering produce to the local market before he was even old enough to reach the pedals properly. He honed his skills weaving through traffic, a baptism by fire that forged his aggressive, no-holds-barred style. His breakthrough came unexpectedly at an amateur race in Interlagos. With a borrowed car and sheer audacity, he outmaneuvered seasoned veterans, earning him a spot with the fledgling Passat Classic B team. While a championship eludes him, those early victories hinted at a brilliance that some say has faded as the years advance, now he remains a formidable, if somewhat unpredictable, presence on the track, a reminder of his explosive early potential.
drivingStyle: Vianna's driving style is a volatile mix of raw talent and barely contained aggression. He's known for his late braking and audacious overtaking maneuvers, often pushing his car, and his rivals, to the absolute limit. While his tire management has improved over the years, he still tends to favor outright speed over strategic conservation, a trait that sometimes costs him dearly in longer races. Under pressure, Vianna either excels, channeling his intensity into blistering pace, or cracks, making rash decisions that send him spiraling down the order.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the 2018 Curitiba Grand Prix, where Silva accused Vianna of deliberately wrecking him.
A fierce on-track rivalry fueled by their contrasting driving styles – Flores' calculated precision versus Vianna's reckless abandon.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific old samba song before every race to calm his nerves.
Insists on personally inspecting his tires before they're mounted on the car.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. Out there, you either win, or you crash trying."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2017 Tarumã 300 in dominant fashion, leading from pole position and setting a new lap record, silencing critics who doubted his ability to perform under pressure.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2020 Cascavel de Ouro, handing victory to his arch-rival Ricardo Silva and facing intense media scrutiny.
